lines.text: It already has.
Nothing changes. Its warmth still reaches your skin.
Its last light is still on the way.
Sunlight takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us.
Then the sky goes out.
1.3 seconds later, the Moon goes dark too.
It never had light of its own.
But Jupiter keeps shining for over an hour.
Its last sunlight is still crossing space.
Gravity also moves at the speed of light.
For 8 minutes, Earth kept circling a Sun that was gone.
Now it flies off in a straight line.
Plants stop making food at once.
One week: −18 °C.
One year: −73 °C.
The oceans freeze over.
But ice is a blanket.
Below it, the deep ocean stays liquid.
Warmed by Earth's own heat.
Life at hot vents never needed sunlight.
Millions of years later: −238 °C.
The air itself freezes, and falls as snow.
Earth still spins. A day still lasts 24 hours.
There's just no day.
And for 8 minutes and 20 seconds… no one would know.
